rows.description: She chooses a different stream than he advised and fears his disappointment. A wise mentor says "I would have chosen otherwise, but I trust your reasons," and the bond becomes more equal.
graph_context: next stage: Boundaries and a lasting thread
this subtopic also appears at ages: 23–26
related mind states: disappointment, fear, trust

rows.subtype: Stage 6: Boundaries and a lasting thread [Response]
rows.description: The mentor keeps relations professional and open, with others aware, so the guidance stays safe. Any adult who asks for secrecy, gifts or private contact beyond the role should prompt the teen to tell a parent or other trusted adult.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 23–26

rows.description: A junior employee, unsure of her path, asks a senior colleague for coffee. She wants both practical answers and a sense that someone experienced believes she can succeed.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17

rows.description: The senior shares her own early failures and a few honest details about office politics. Honest stories of struggle make the mentee feel less alone and more willing to be candid.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17

rows.description: The mentor tells her that she speaks too little in meetings and gives examples. It stings, and the mentee must decide whether to defend or absorb what is useful.
graph_context: next stage: The mentee outgrows some advice
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17

rows.subtype: Stage 4: The mentee outgrows some advice [Receiver]
rows.description: She disagrees with a suggestion based on how the industry worked ten years ago. Feeling both loyal and doubtful, she needs the courage to say so respectfully, and the mentor the humility to hear it.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17

rows.description: The mentor feels a touch of hurt when the mentee's success passes hers, then chooses pride over rivalry. Great mentors count the success of others as part of their own work and are glad to be needed less.
graph_context: previous stage: The mentee outgrows some advice
next stage: Peer and paying it forward
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17
related mind states: joy, pride, hurt

rows.subtype: Stage 6: Peer and paying it forward [Response]
rows.description: The relationship turns into a friendship of equals, and the mentee starts guiding someone newer. The circle continues when gratitude is expressed through passing on the help received.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17

rows.description: A young man feels his father has always compared him to cousins and dismissed his interest in art. Years of small wounds build a belief that he can never be accepted as he is.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 23–26

rows.description: After a harsh argument over his course, he moves out and says he does not wish to be contacted. Part of him is relieved and part is terrified, and pride makes the decision feel final.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 23–26
